alexcrichton opened PR #14502 from alexcrichton:refactor-winch-features to bytecodealliance:main:

I've realized locally that in addition to removing the gc-types/exceptions defaults we should also be removing tail-call by default. To handle that I've decided to refactor this slightly to explicitly enable features for Winch instead of disabling them from Cranelift's features. This should be a bit more robust over time because if we add something to Cranelift's set we don't have to remember to remove it from Winch's set.

:thumbs_up: cfallin submitted PR review:

Some thoughts below but I'm not strongly attached either way; just my idea/impression...

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

Would it be a little easier to follow if we had something like

let mut features = WasmFeatures::empty();
match self.compiler_config.as_ref().and_then(|c| c.strategy) {
  // XXX does `None` mean Cranelift or no compilation?
  None => {
    features |= WasmFeatures::WASM3 | WasmFeatures::WIDE_ARITHMETIC;
  }

  #[cfg(feature = "cranelift")]
  Some(Strategy::CraneliftNative) | Some(Strategy::CraneliftPulley) => {
    features |= WasmFeatures::WASM3 | WasmFeatures::WIDE_ARITHMETIC;
  }

  #[cfg(feature = "winch")]
  Some(Strategy::Winch) => {
    features |= WasmFeatures::WASM2 | ...;
    features.remove(WasmFeatures::GC_TYPES);
  }
}

(I'm not as familiar with this code as you but at least naively, it feels like there should be a table-by-compiler somewhere rather than an "overwrite earlier value" flow)
